uniequip_002_chen2:
Looking at the boy in front of her, Ch'en is somewhat taken aback.
'Your mother? Smuggling?'
'Yes. But she was forced into it by my dad.'
'And you want me to save her?'
'My dad and his associates will be waiting for her in the square.'
'How do you know that?'
'...I used to be the one helping him with this.' The boy gritted his teeth. 'My dad once promised that after making enough money, he'd take my mom and me on a cruise, and we could see a rainbow over the sea from there. But he never kept his word. He just kept chasing dirty money, forcing me to work with him, and now he wants to drag my mom down with him too. I can't stand it anymore.'
Ch'en notices bruises on the boy's neck. With her years of experience, she instantly knew he was telling the truth.
'...Don't worry. If what you say is true, I'll make sure your father and his crew get the punishment they deserve.'
At the word 'punishment,' the boy, who had kept his head down, suddenly looks up. 'Does prison really change people?'
'...Why do you ask?'
'My dad wasn't like this before. Ever since we came to Dossoles, he's been obsessed with making money. I don't even know when he changed... maybe he's always been this way. But I can't forget the look in his eyes when he first told me he'd take me on a cruise to see a rainbow.'
Looking at the boy, Ch'en is reminded of her past self. Back then, she had always wanted a certain someone to notice her sword. But at some point, she stopped hoping for that.
'This city is surrounded by water. Rainbows should be easy to find here. Haven't you seen enough of them?'
'...No. I have to see a rainbow with him, on a cruise; nothing else counts.'
Yes, it only counts if he's there.
'Hah. And you still want that, even now?'
'Yeah.' There is a faint glimmer of hope in the boy's eyes, but it quickly fades. 'But I can't do it alone.'
Ch'en is silent for a moment, then grabs her water gun and walks in the direction the boy had indicated. Before going, she leaves him with a final piece of advice.
'Then you'll have to find a way to make your father listen to you. Make him understand that you want him to change... At the very least, let him know what you're thinking.'
That day, there was a sudden downpour in Dossoles. In the rain, Ch'en saved a woman from a group of criminals and subdued the culprits.
Strangely, just as the gang leader was about to fight back, a child suddenly stepped between him and Ch'en. The rain had stopped at some point, and a rainbow arched across the sky. Beneath it, the gang leader hesitated, and the child seemed to say something to him. Finally, the leader lowered his weapon.
Witnesses nearby reported that, although Ch'en had successfully resolved another smuggling case, she didn't seem happy. She simply looked off to the east, lost in thought.
uniequip_003_chen2:
There's still a slight chill in the morning air. Ch'en is helping Mikhail split firewood.
She looks at the pile of wood at her feet. 'That should be enough.'
She exhales, loosens her shoulders, and starts thinking about what to do next.
This morning she'll stop by the newly repaired workshop and bake cookies with Svetlana, as she promised.
And then... Well, Mikhail has invited her to his house for lunch. She plans to ask the old artificer to fix her Steam Knight model while she's there—it was a gift from a Victorian.
In the afternoon, she and Mikhail are going to check the fields, which, unfortunately, are plagued by insects. The two of them have spent days figuring out how to modify her water-gun to spray pesticides, and today is the day to test out their invention.
In the evening... ah, right, the Messenger is coming to town today, which means the letter from Dossoles should have arrived. The people there are even nicer than she expected. They often write to her with updates. She intends to draw up a new training plan for them. And of course, she should write a letter to Madam Fumizuki to let her know she's safe.
'So much to do, so little time.' With that thought, she takes a step forward, when a young man blocks her way.
It's Svetlana's son, a member of the town's defense corps. Some time ago, Ch'en had helped out with some work for the defense corps. Ever since then, the young boy had been begging her to take him on as a disciple.
'Tell me how I can become strong like you, Miss Ch'en!' he says.
'Go back and keep swinging your sword every day,' is her reply.
She is not deceiving him.
Sword practice was once the most important thing in Ch'en Hui-chieh's life. Back when she lived in Lungmen, she always found time to train, regardless of the weather, and no matter how many other duties had piled up.
'But you've been living in our town for so long, and I've never once seen you practice.'
His words catch her off guard. She suddenly realizes she really hasn't practiced in quite a while.
At some point, she's not sure when, sword practice no longer seemed as important—or rather, as pressing to her as it once did. Today's list of errands feels just as important to her as sword practice.
It suddenly dawns on her—the old Ch'en Hui-chieh would never have thought this way.
But when she thinks of that younger her, always with something to prove, she finds within herself a confidence that she finds hard to explain.
Chi Xiao must be sharper than ever.
No, her sword must be sharper than ever.
'Shall I give you a demonstration?'
'Huh?'
Ch'en shifts her stance ever so slightly. Miraculously, a 'sword' appears in her hands, seemingly out of thin air.
This 'sword' gives the young boy an overwhelming sense of foreboding. He feels an urge to run, but finds himself unable to move, forced to watch as the 'sword' swings toward him. Reflexively, he shuts his eyes.
Of course, the 'sword' does not strike him. Instead, Ch'en only pats his shoulder.
'Come on. Your mother is waiting for us.'
The young man opens his eyes. Off in the distance, his mother, Svetlana, is waving to them from the ridge, calling them over to the workshop. Ch'en walks toward her, and the boy hurries after her.
'Miss Ch'en, if I keep swinging my sword every day, will I be able to do what you just did?' he asks, his voice teeming with excitement.
'No. Just swinging your sword is not enough. You must also walk many, many miles.'
Ch'en lifts her head to the sky. The sun is shining brightly today. A fine day for a journey.
